framing_note: A document-native read of TMICC's own filings, organized by fiscal year rather than by document — one entry per year, each showing that year's real dated checkpoints and financial figures, with page/item citations back to whichever filing actually covers it. Distinct from the Strategy tab (which back-traces commitments to initiatives) and the Timeline tab (which correlates TMICC against competitors/macro events). Honesty note: TMICC itself has only ever filed one true Annual Report (FY2025) — it only began independent existence in Dec 2025. FY2022-2024 are not separate 'annual reports'; they're combined carve-out financial statements for the Ice Cream Business, extracted from TMICC's own pre-listing SEC registration statement (Form 20FR12B, filed 4 Nov 2025), which is the real document that carries this history. Labeled by year for the strategist's mental model, sourced honestly underneath.

source_document.title: The Magnum Ice Cream Company N.V. — Annual Report 2025
source_document.filing_type: Form 20-F (Annual Report), filed with the U.S. SEC — the SEC's annual-report equivalent for a foreign private issuer. TMICC is Netherlands-incorporated and listed on NYSE, LSE, and Euronext Amsterdam, so it files a 20-F rather than a US-domestic 10-K; functionally the same disclosure role, which is why this panel is framed as a 10-K-style analyzer.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Reorganisation anchor date — the ice cream business's internal restructuring within Unilever, ahead of the demerger
strategic_checkpoints.detail: The base date the standalone-group reorganisation is anchored to.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Pro forma capitalisation at listing: €587m cash, €4,049m total indebtedness, €2,143m share capital
strategic_checkpoints.detail: The balance-sheet snapshot used to size TMICC's opening capital structure ahead of listing — compare against year-end's actual €3,416m financial liabilities below.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Interim combined carve-out results: revenue €4,503m (H1 2024: €4,394m), operating profit €569m (H1 2024: €608m), net profit €464m
strategic_checkpoints.detail: Revenue grew +2.5% year-on-year but operating profit fell -6.4% — margin compression in the run-up to listing, worth watching against the full FY2025 figures once available.
strategic_checkpoints.cross_reference: Registration statement, Combined Carve-Out Income Statement

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: €500 million productivity programme
strategic_checkpoints.detail: Three levers named explicitly: supply chain transformation, overhead reduction, and technology-enabled operations. Designed to deliver savings over the medium term.
strategic_checkpoints.cross_reference: Strategy tab — headline commitment 'Cost / separation savings'

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Demerger from Unilever completed; TMICC began trading as an independent listed company
strategic_checkpoints.detail: Described in both the Board Chair and CEO updates as the defining milestone of the year.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: €3 billion debut bond issuance across four tranches (2029, 2031, 2034, 2037)
strategic_checkpoints.detail: Euro Medium Term Note programme, interest rate range 2.75%-4%, order book oversubscribed more than 7x. Financial liabilities rose to €3,416m (2024: €333m); average debt maturity 7.5 years — TMICC's real debt-maturity wall.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: India demerger expected effective; Kwality Wall's India expected to start trading by April 2026
strategic_checkpoints.detail: India was a Deferred Territory — not part of the main December 2025 demerger, following its own separate timeline. (For comparison: the actual completion tracked in Ecosystem/Strategy was 30 March 2026 — close to, but later than, this original expectation.)
strategic_checkpoints.cross_reference: Ecosystem/Strategy tabs — Kwality Wall's, AMEA / India expansion

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Portugal demerger expected effective; Portugal asset sale has up to 3 years from the share sale to complete
strategic_checkpoints.detail: Portugal was the other named Deferred Territory alongside India — two separate milestones for the same territory.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: €300 million credit facility earmarked for the Indian ice cream business acquisition
strategic_checkpoints.detail: Financing detail behind the Kwality Wall's transaction — the specific facility funding it.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Full compliance with the 2025 Dutch Corporate Governance Code, Best Practice Provision 1.4.3(ii)-(iv)
strategic_checkpoints.detail: TMICC's own Board states it is not yet fully compliant as a newly-standalone company, and expects to close the gap by 2026 — distinct from the Foundation Plan for Growth shareholder-dissent issue tracked in the Timeline.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Exit all remaining Transitional Services Agreements (TSAs) with Unilever
strategic_checkpoints.detail: TMICC still relies on Unilever for some transitional operational support post-demerger; full independence is targeted for end-2027.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Vanilla for Change programme — 80% of enrolled Madagascar farmers transitioned to regenerative agriculture; 1 million trees planted (up from 585,000 today), survival rate target rising from 40% to 65%
strategic_checkpoints.detail: Run with Symrise and Save the Children in the vanilla-producing Sava region of Madagascar.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: New cabinet energy-efficiency technology begins rolling out on new freezer-cabinet purchases
strategic_checkpoints.detail: Connects directly to the freezer-cabinet fleet risk already flagged in Ecosystem (TMICC's largest single emissions source, a fleet it doesn't own).

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Net Zero ambition across Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions
strategic_checkpoints.detail: Explicit scenario-planning horizons defined elsewhere: near-term 2026-2030, medium-term 2031-2039.

clarifications.clarification: Appears only inside the standard forward-looking-statements disclaimer boilerplate (a list of example statement categories), not as a fresh disclosure. Most plausibly refers to the already-known Kwality Wall's transaction rather than a second, undisclosed India deal.

documents.label: FY2024

source_document.title: Combined Carve-Out Financial Statements (Ice Cream Business), FY2024
source_document.filing_type: Not a standalone annual report — figures from the Combined Carve-Out Income Statement and Balance Sheet inside TMICC's pre-listing SEC registration statement (Form 20FR12B). TMICC did not exist as a separate filer in 2024; these are Unilever's ice cream business carved out and restated as if independent.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Combined carve-out revenue: €7,947m
strategic_checkpoints.detail: +4.3% vs FY2023's €7,618m — reported revenue growth from the raw carve-out figures, not TMICC's own constant-currency 'organic sales growth' non-IFRS metric (which isn't disclosed for these carve-out years). The strongest of the three carve-out years.
strategic_checkpoints.cross_reference: Registration statement, Combined Carve-Out Income Statement

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Operating profit €764m (9.6% margin)
strategic_checkpoints.detail: +3.0% vs FY2023's €742m — profit grew slightly slower than revenue, margin ticked down from 9.7% to 9.6%.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Net profit €595m
strategic_checkpoints.detail: +16.9% vs FY2023's €509m — a real rebound, driven by no hyperinflation monetary loss in 2024 (vs a €10m loss in 2023) and higher operating profit.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Regional split: Europe and ANZ €3.1bn (39% of revenue), Americas €2.9bn (36%)
strategic_checkpoints.detail: Implies AMEA at roughly €1.9bn (~25%, a residual computed here, not directly disclosed at this granularity). 70% of Group revenue came from developed markets, 30% from emerging markets.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Goodwill and intangible assets roughly doubled: goodwill €272m to €585m, intangibles €381m to €793m
strategic_checkpoints.detail: A real, dated balance-sheet signal consistent with a meaningful acquisition somewhere in this window — the specific transaction wasn't identified in this pass.

gaps_not_found_this_pass: The specific acquisition(s) behind the FY2022-2024 goodwill/intangibles increase weren't identified.
No disclosed constant-currency organic sales growth % for this year — only reported revenue growth could be computed.

documents.label: FY2023

source_document.title: Combined Carve-Out Financial Statements (Ice Cream Business), FY2023
source_document.filing_type: Not a standalone annual report — figures from the Combined Carve-Out Income Statement inside TMICC's pre-listing SEC registration statement (Form 20FR12B).

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Combined carve-out revenue: €7,618m
strategic_checkpoints.detail: +1.5% vs FY2022's €7,506m — the weakest revenue growth of the three carve-out years.
strategic_checkpoints.cross_reference: Registration statement, Combined Carve-Out Income Statement

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Operating profit €742m (9.7% margin)
strategic_checkpoints.detail: +0.7% vs FY2022's €737m — essentially flat, margin ticked down slightly from 9.8%.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Net profit fell to €509m despite higher revenue
strategic_checkpoints.detail: -3.4% vs FY2022's €527m. The real drivers: a €10m net monetary loss from hyperinflationary economies (vs €2m in 2022), and taxation rising to €203m (vs €173m in 2022) even though profit before tax was higher. Worth noting for a strategist: revenue growth alone didn't carry through to the bottom line this year.
